question: Do extrinsic input dimension, manifold dimension, or task-relevant dimension explain how much iterative magnitude pruning a network tolerates?

key_findings.claim: Changing pixel resolution has only a weak association with prunability under the tested ResNet20 setup.
key_findings.evidence: Nearest-neighbor resizing CIFAR-10 from 16x16 to 128x128 while holding convolutional parameter count fixed yields average Spearman correlation -0.22 between dimension and weights remaining, indicating only slightly greater pruning at higher resolution.

key_findings.claim: Lower BigGAN latent dimension correlates with greater prunability in generated image datasets.
key_findings.evidence: Masking latent coordinates to 16, 32, 64, or 128 dimensions produces average Spearman correlation 0.74 between latent dimension and weights remaining across three ResNet20 widths.

key_findings.claim: Synthetic task dimension has no measurable pruning effect in the linear-classification construction.
key_findings.evidence: With intrinsic dimension 128 and extrinsic dimension 1024 fixed, varying label dependence over 16-128 coordinates gives correlation 0.01 and nearly overlapping IMP curves for three two-layer MLP sizes.

method.core_idea: Intervene on one notion of data dimension at a time, then measure the smallest iterative-magnitude-pruned subnetwork matching dense test accuracy.
method.mechanism: CIFAR resizing changes extrinsic dimension, BigGAN latent masking approximates intrinsic dimension, and a projected linear synthetic dataset varies task-relevant coordinates; weight-rewinding IMP generates pruning curves.
assumptions: BigGAN active latent coordinates are a useful proxy and upper bound for true manifold dimension.
Matching dense accuracy is a stable and comparable definition of prunability.
IMP with rewinding represents pruning methods more broadly.

techniques.role: Attempts to isolate extrinsic, intrinsic, and task dimensions experimentally.
Measures maximum removable weight fraction under one standardized procedure.
Propagates pruning-rate uncertainty into rank-correlation estimates.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 resized across four spatial resolutions and three ResNet20 widths
evaluations.metric: Minimum weights remaining and Spearman correlation
evaluations.result: Extrinsic dimension has weak negative correlation (-0.22) with weights remaining.

evaluations.setting: BigGAN-generated images with four active latent dimensions
evaluations.result: Higher latent dimension requires more weights, correlation 0.74, although several estimates have large variance.
evaluations.baseline: Same ResNet20 widths across latent masks

evaluations.setting: Projected linear classification with varied task dimension
evaluations.result: Curves nearly overlap and correlation is 0.01.
evaluations.baseline: Fixed intrinsic/extrinsic dimensions and varied relevant coordinates

limitations: This preliminary workshop study uses one pruning algorithm, small ResNet20/MLP models, and limited synthetic controls.
BigGAN latent dimension is only an upper bound on data intrinsic dimension and changing active coordinates can change distribution difficulty.
The task-dimension test is linear and synthetic, while pruning thresholds inherit uncertainty from dense accuracy and discrete pruning steps.
failure_modes: Apparent dimension effects can be caused by accuracy, generator, interpolation, or architecture changes rather than dimension itself.
High variance in matching sparsity makes rank ordering unstable for some latent settings.
A conclusion for IMP with rewinding may reverse for structured, one-shot, movement, or post-training pruning.
reusable_insights: Define prunability relative to dense accuracy, but also report absolute sparse accuracy and uncertainty.
Separate ambient, manifold, and target-function complexity rather than using 'dimension' ambiguously.
Treat generator latent size as an intervention proxy and validate it with independent intrinsic-dimension estimators.
open_questions: Does measured intrinsic dimension predict prunability on natural image, text, and audio distributions?
Which pruning algorithms and architectures preserve or reverse the observed correlation?
Can theory link data manifold complexity, approximation error, and the size of a matching subnetwork?

competitive_landscape.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Lottery Ticket demonstrates matching sparse subnetworks and motivates rewinding; this study asks which properties of the input distribution alter their attainable sparsity.

competitive_landscape.title: The State of Sparsity in Deep Neural Networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Gale et al. compare sparsification methods and scales on practical tasks; this paper holds the method fixed to isolate controlled data-dimensionality interventions.

competitive_landscape.title: On the Predictability of Pruning Across Scales
competitive_landscape.difference: Rosenfeld et al. model how pruning outcomes scale with model/data size; this work studies manifold and task dimensions at nominally fixed dataset size and architecture.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: matching subnetworks and pruning scaling are established. The contribution is a clean three-way conceptual decomposition of input dimension and preliminary controlled evidence that BigGAN latent dimension, but not task dimension, correlates with IMP prunability.
reviewer_notes: All ten pages, appendix tables, correlations, and experimental definitions were checked. Primary competitor records checked 2026-08-23. The intrinsic-dimension finding should be read as a BigGAN latent-mask result, not a validated natural-data law.
